newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude hits new post-Gulf War high.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude hits new post-Gulf War high.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures for prompt delivery posted a new post-Gulf War high of $24.75 a barrel in mid-afternoon trade on Monday, beating last Tuesday's high of $24.70.

Tehran earlier denied it was backing the forces of the anti-Baghdad Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) which, according to U.N. officials, has regained most of the territory it lost to the rival Kurdistan Democractic Party (KDP) five weeks ago.

Baghdad's backing of the KDP's offensive last month prompted the U.N. to delay indefinitely the limited oil-for-food sale plan which would have released some 700,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude onto the market.
Since then, world prices have drawn strong support from low stocks of heating oil ahead of the northern hemisphere winter.
News that a fire on Saturday at British Petroleum's refinery in Toledo, Ohio had reduced throughput was also helping U.S. product markets on Monday, dealers said.
IPE Nov gas oil was $7.00 a tonne firmer at $233.50 a tonne by 1523 GMT. -- Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
